name: Bladee
label: Trash Island
lede: Benjamin Reichwald wanted to be a painter, sang through Auto-Tune instead, and in 2024 left his label and put out the album Pitchfork ranked No. 8 of the year.

eras.title: A painter's kid from Skanstull
eras.text: Benjamin Reichwald grows up in Stockholm wanting to paint, and by the time he's a teenager he's making noise with his classmate Zak Gaterud, years before either is Bladee or Ecco2k.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bladee · The FADER: Being Bladee
years.h: Benjamin Reichwald, future Bladee, is born in Stockholm
years.p: Full name Benjamin Thage Dag Reichwald. He grows up in Skanstull and wants to be a painter.
years.xp: The FADER and Wikipedia agree on the household: his mother was a schoolteacher and his father worked in restaurants. His younger brother Gus later shoots many Drain Gang and Sad Boys videos.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bladee · Wikipedia: Drain Gang · The FADER: Being Bladee
years.h: Krossad, a kids' punk band with Ecco2k
years.p: Reichwald and [[Ecco2k|66ab36ce-8f58-46fb-9284-396c2c90ecbd]] name it after the Swedish word for "crushed" and put out a demo CD in 2007.
years.xp:
Sources disagree on the details. Wikipedia dates the band to 2004 and the demo to 2007; the Drain Gang article calls it a grindcore duo from 2008, when both were thirteen; the FADER has Bladee forming a punk band with Ecco2k at 11.

His own description to the FADER: "We were just basically making noise. We didn't know how to play music at all."

eras.title: Gravity Boys, Shield Gang, Drain Gang
eras.text: Three Stockholm friends and a beatmaker pile onto SoundCloud, can't settle on a name, and fall in beside Yung Lean's Sad Boys.

years.src: Wikipedia: Drain Gang · The FADER: Being Bladee
years.h: The crew cycles through names until Drain Gang sticks
years.p: [[Bladee|cd689e77-dfdd-4f81-b50c-5e5a3f5e38a4]], [[Ecco2k|66ab36ce-8f58-46fb-9284-396c2c90ecbd]], [[Thaiboy Digital|68d311c0-525f-4f72-a044-84e54565d02d]] and producer [[Whitearmor|984e5e75-e483-4670-ac53-9b5f28222437]] try Gravity Boys, then Shield Gang.
years.xp:
Bladee met Whitearmor and Thaiboy through mutual friends, and they started freestyling on Whitearmor's beats for fun. The plan, as he told the FADER, was to "just sing in Auto-Tune." Wikipedia quotes him on the name: drain is about loss and gain, good or bad, and everything he and his friends do connects to that idea.

The sound, Auto-Tune over cold synths, fit the melancholy of Stockholm's Sad Boys, and the two crews fused.

years.src: The FADER: Being Bladee · Wikipedia: Drain Gang
years.h: Yung Lean's mixtape lets Bladee in on "Heal You // Bladerunner"
years.p: The guest spot on Unknown Death 2002 ties Gravity Boys to Sad Boys for good.
years.xp: Bladee and Whitearmor had heard Lean's "Greygoose" and reached out, the FADER reports. The mixtape came out in 2013.

years.h: Gluee is the first mixtape under the Bladee name
years.p: Wikipedia calls it an anthem for a suburban generation stuck scrolling Twitter.
years.xp: Whitearmor is already in the production chair, a partnership that runs through to Sulfur Surfer in 2026.

eras.title: Year0001 signs everyone
eras.text: A Stockholm label takes the whole crew, Whitearmor builds Bladee's first real album, and one member can't come on tour.

years.cap: Bladee at The Hoxton, Toronto, March 2016
years.h: Eversince is Whitearmor from start to finish
years.p: Out through Year0001, with Ripsquadd and Hitkidd in support.
years.xp:
Vice's Craig Jenkins heard modern rap, R&B, gothic and new wave in it; Gaffa's Jonathan Eklund called it a brilliant debut that stepped Bladee out of Yung Lean's shadow.

Physical copies took years: a Swedish CD in 2019, a US LP in 2022, a European LP in 2023.

years.h: Year0001 signs the whole crew
years.p: The Stockholm label was co-founded by Oskar Ekman and Emilio Fagone, Yung Lean's manager.

years.src: Wikipedia: Drain Gang · The FADER: The album that sparked
years.h: The first big tour goes out without Thaiboy Digital
years.p: Bladee, [[Ecco2k|66ab36ce-8f58-46fb-9284-396c2c90ecbd]] and [[Whitearmor|984e5e75-e483-4670-ac53-9b5f28222437]] play the Eversince Tour without him; he can't enter the EU after a 2015 deportation from Sweden.
years.xp: Wikipedia puts the tour at eight dates, November to December 2016, and says Thaiboy was kept out by EU visa issues. The FADER adds that Trash Island was recorded in Thailand in part because he couldn't return to Sweden.

years.h: The 2016 election brings a fandom nobody wanted
years.p: Drain Gang picks up an alt-right following that the members reject.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the members reject right-wing and white supremacist ideologies. Writer Cassidy George of 032c put it this way: the group's suffering, specific to the internet age, "has bred a fandom encompassing the two most extreme poles" of politics. Later queer themes, notably the 2020 video for "Amygdala", widened the audience.

years.src: Wikipedia: Working on Dying · Wikipedia: Bladee
years.h: Working on Dying pairs Bladee with a Philadelphia collective
years.p: Yung Lean and Ecco2k guest on a mixtape named for the production crew behind it.
years.xp: Working on Dying was founded in 2012 by the brothers F1lthy and Oogie Mane, known for high-tempo 808s. F1lthy goes on to do most of the production on Cold Visions.

eras.title: Lightning, then a record about it
eras.text: Runways, a trip to Thailand that Bladee says changed how he saw everything, and a surprise album made there.

years.h: Gud, Whitearmor and Yung Sherman run Red Light
years.p: They executive produce his second album, which includes the single "Decay".

years.src: WKNC: Bladee's Cold Visions · Wikipedia: Bladee
years.h: Icedancer closes the year with Ripsquadd on the boards
years.p: A year-end mixtape with Yung Lean and Thaiboy Digital on it.
years.xp: Fans often group Icedancer with Working on Dying when they say Cold Visions feels like a return to form, as one WKNC critic put it.

years.big: "I was sure I was gonna die, but I didn't."
q: I was sure I was gonna die, but I didn't.
years.src: The FADER: Being Bladee · Wikipedia: Bladee
years.h: Lightning finds Bladee in Thailand
years.p: He says a strike hit him on a trip there; Wikipedia dates it to 2019 and calls it transformative.
years.xp:
In the FADER's 2019 interview he says the strike "put me into this next level of seeing things."

The same piece lays out the Trash Island worldview: the world is a trash island, and you have the power to create your own reality.

years.cap: Bladee, Ecco2k, Thaiboy Digital and Whitearmor
years.src: The FADER: The album that sparked · Wikipedia: Drain Gang
yt: Drain Gang live in NYC, full set
years.h: No announcement, then Trash Island
years.p: Drain Gang's 22-minute, eight-track album comes out of Thailand, where Thaiboy Digital could work after being kept out of Sweden.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says it was partly recorded and produced in Bangkok. The FADER calls it the group's tightest project and the one that took them past cult status.

Solo records followed fast: Thaiboy's Legendary Member two weeks later and Ecco2k's E two months after.

eras.title: Prolific, then loud
eras.text: Three records in 2020, a gallery show, a joint album with Ecco2k and a US tour; Drain Gang starts turning up in Dazed and Rolling Stone.

years.h: Exeter comes out of one week on Gotland
years.p: Nine songs, 18 minutes 21 seconds, the shortest Bladee album to date, and his first big run with producer Gud.
years.xp: Pitchfork's Ben Dandridge-Lemco gave it 7.2 and called it the sort of album that rewards leaning in, per Wikipedia. Anthony Fantano gave it a 5.

years.h: Three months later, a surprise drop called 333
years.p: Whitearmor executive produces the record, named for Drain Gang's holy number, three.

years.h: Good Luck goes EDM, and Charli XCX remixes "Drama"
years.p: Bladee premieres the Mechatok-made record by livestream; the deluxe edition carries [[Charli XCX|260b6184-8828-48eb-945c-bc4cb6fc34ca]]'s remix.

years.h: The Fool turns to pop rap, with Lusi
years.p: Pitchfork's Nadine Smith gave it 7.7; The FADER ranked it No. 11 of 2021.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits Lusi with most of the production and describes a turn toward introspection and spiritual questions. Dazed placed it 14th on its year-end list.

years.h: A painter's kid gets a gallery show in London
years.p: Real Sprin9 hangs at Residence Gallery through August.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Drain Gang Interview · Wikipedia: Bladee
yt: Drain Gang live at The Hollywood
years.h: Crest, then sold-out nights in Queens
years.p: Bladee and Ecco2k's joint album is all Whitearmor, and it sends them out on a US tour.
years.xp: Rolling Stone called it a soaring and rapturous triumph. Its piece on the first US Drain Gang tour describes rain falling on the crowd before the show and the room erupting like a blissed-out exorcism. Bladee: "We've never compromised on that."

years.h: Spiderr is the sixth solo album
years.p: Ecco2k directs the video. Wikipedia describes mixed reception, the backdrop to Cold Visions.

eras.title: Alone in the house
eras.text: Skrillex, a record with Yung Lean, then a surprise album made in his own Stockholm house that lands at No. 8 on Pitchfork's 2024 list.

yt: Resident Advisor interview: Drain Gang, new music, Skrillex
years.h: Skrillex brings in Bladee for "Real Spring" and "Ceremony"
years.p: Two singles in two months; Yung Lean is on the second.

yt: Yung Lean and Bladee, Boiler Room London
years.h: Bladee and Yung Lean release Psykos with no warning
years.p: Palmistry and Silent$ky produce the 8-track, 22-minute World Affairs release.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls it their first collaborative album after more than a decade of working together, recorded across Thailand and Sweden. Pitchfork gave it 8.0 and The Needle Drop a 5.

years.src: Album of the Year: Cold Visions · Wikipedia: Cold Visions · WKNC: Bladee's Cold Visions
years.h: Cold Visions arrives on a Tuesday night, 30 tracks long
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.3, Best New Music, and ranked it No. 8 of 2024; The FADER put it at No. 4.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Bladee made it in about two weeks at his house in Stockholm, in a depressive stretch as he approached 30, with the reception of Spiderr on his mind. Kieran Press-Reynolds' review, as quoted by AOTY and Wikipedia, called it "the most fully realized project of his career".

F1lthy handles most production, with Yung Lean, Yung Sherman, Thaiboy Digital and Black Kray appearing; Ecco2k does not. Wikipedia lists it as his first solo release outside Year0001.

years.h: Harmony Korine's EDGLRD directs the "One Second" video
years.p: [[Yung Lean|757ed661-fbad-4e45-b1cd-a6b09f06f54a]] guests on the second single from Cold Visions.

years.cap: III Points Festival 2024 lineup poster, Miami, October 2024
yt: Bladee and Yung Lean, One Second (live)
years.h: "One Second" gets a live run at III Points
years.p: Bladee and Yung Lean play the Cold Visions single at the festival.

years.big: "I don't owe them my next five projects."
q: A lot of stuff wasn't what we thought it was.
years.src: The FADER: Bladee discusses · Wikipedia: Drain Gang
years.h: Drain Gang walks out of Year0001
years.p: Bladee, Ecco2k, Thaiboy Digital, Gud and Yung Lean all part from the label in 2024.
years.xp:
In a February 2025 FADER interview Bladee said that when they got a lawyer, "a lot of things were not in order or standard." Of the split: "It was not a personal decision, but a professional one."

Year0001 co-founder Emilio Fagone's version: "All we got was a very long letter from a lawyer."

eras.title: Saint George
eras.text: Free of Year0001, Bladee puts out a three-song EP on his own label, tours ten countries and keeps the run going.

years.h: A flag-wrapped sword in a graveyard, and a surprise EP
years.p: Ste the Beautiful Martyr 1st Attempt runs 7:47 over three tracks on Bladee's own Trash Island label.
years.xp: Kieran Press-Reynolds read the Saint George imagery as a fight against the evil things in Bladee's mind and called the opener "One in a Million" textbook Bladee.

yt: Drain Gang at Avicii Arena, Stockholm, March 2025
years.h: The Martyr World Tour starts, his biggest yet
years.p: Announced in May across 10 countries, it begins in October 2025.

years.cap: Whitearmor DJing at Outset, Chicago, June 4, 2026
years.h: Sulfur Surfer, produced entirely by Whitearmor
years.p: His eleventh solo project, which Wikipedia says was inspired by ego death and the feeling of mid-transformation.
